name: Garlic-Butter Salmon & Crispy Potatoes
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Put the potatoes on a sheet pan. Toss with 4 tsp olive oil, 1 tsp seasoned salt, and the black pepper. Roast cut-side down for 15 minutes.
Push the potatoes to one side. Add the green beans and toss them with the remaining 2 tsp olive oil and a pinch of seasoned salt.
Pat the salmon dry. Mix melted butter, garlic, garlic powder, smoked paprika, and the remaining seasoned salt. Spoon it over the salmon.
Place salmon on the pan and bake everything 10–12 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily and reaches 125–130°F for moist salmon or 145°F for fully cooked.
Squeeze lemon over the salmon and green beans. Plate it hot.
note: Flaky salmon with a rich garlic-butter finish, balanced with fresh lemon and crisp roasted potatoes.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.
prep: Protein — 4 salmon fillets, 5–6 oz each.
Sauce / finish — 2 tbsp butter, melted.

name: Loaded Cheeseburger Rice Skillet
prep: Beef: Have 1 1/2 lb 88/12 ground beef ready. Dice 1/2 onion.
Seasoning: Measure 1 tsp seasoned salt, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp onion powder, and 1/2 tsp black pepper.
Rice: Rinse 1 cup jasmine rice and measure 2 cups beef broth.
Finish: Measure 1 tbsp ketchup, 1 tsp yellow mustard, and 1 1/2 cups shredded cheddar. Have dill pickle slices ready if using.
steps: Heat a deep skillet over medium-high. Add 1 1/2 lb ground beef and the diced 1/2 onion. Cook 7–9 minutes, breaking up the beef, until browned. Drain excess grease if needed.
Stir in 1 tsp seasoned salt, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp onion powder, and 1/2 tsp black pepper.
Add 1 cup rinsed jasmine rice and 2 cups beef broth. Bring to a simmer, cover, reduce heat to low, and cook about 15 minutes, until the rice is tender.
Stir in 1 tbsp ketchup and 1 tsp yellow mustard. Sprinkle 1 1/2 cups cheddar over the top, cover, and let stand about 2 minutes until melted.
Top with dill pickle slices for classic cheeseburger flavor.
note: Seasoned ground beef, rice and melted cheddar with classic cheeseburger flavor.
leftovers: Reheat with a splash of broth.

name: Meaty Spaghetti
ingredients: 4 cups (32 oz) Ragu Old World Style Traditional Sauce
1/4–1/2 tsp crushed red pepper flakes, optional
1 1/2 tbsp salt for the pasta water
1/2 cup reserved pasta water, only as needed
prep: Pot — Pasta: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Have 16 oz spaghetti and 1 1/2 tbsp salt ready.
Skillet/Dutch oven — Meat sauce: Dice 1 large yellow onion. Measure the beef, butter, minced garlic, dry seasonings, and 4 cups Ragu.
Before draining pasta: Reserve about 1/2 cup pasta water.
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Add 1 1/2 tbsp salt, then add 16 oz spaghetti. Cook until al dente according to the package directions. Before draining, reserve about 1/2 cup pasta water. Drain; do not rinse.
While the pasta water heats, place a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add 2 lb ground beef. Let it sit undisturbed for 2–3 minutes so the bottom gets a good brown sear.

Break the beef into bite-size crumbles. Add 1 1/2 tsp Italian seasoning, 3/4 tsp garlic powder, 3/4 tsp onion powder, 1/2 tsp black pepper, and 1/4–1/2 tsp crushed red pepper flakes if using. Stir the seasonings through the beef and continue cooking until no pink remains.

Drain the excess grease, leaving about 1 tbsp in the pan. Reduce heat to medium. Add 1 tbsp butter and 1 large diced yellow onion. Cook 4–5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the onion is softened.
Add 2 tbsp minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds, stirring so the garlic does not burn.
Add 4 cups (32 oz) Ragu Old World Style Traditional Sauce and stir well. Bring to a gentle simmer, reduce heat to low, and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.

Add the drained spaghetti to the meat sauce and toss until evenly coated. If it is too thick, add reserved pasta water 1 tbsp at a time, only as needed. Taste the finished spaghetti before adding any extra salt.
note: A thick, rich meat sauce with two pounds of beef, Ragu, garlic, onion and a touch of butter tossed with spaghetti.
leftovers: Refrigerate promptly. Reheat gently with a small splash of water only if the sauce needs loosening.

name: Meaty Three-Cheese Lasagna
ingredients: 2 jars (24 oz each) Ragu Traditional sauce
1 tsp sugar, only if sauce tastes acidic
1/2 tsp garlic powder for cheese mixture
1/2 tsp Italian seasoning for cheese mixture
prep: Pot — Noodles: Boil 12 noodles just to al dente; drain and lay flat.
Skillet — Sauce: Dice onion; measure beef, garlic, seasonings and Ragu.
Bowl — Cheese: Mix ricotta, egg, 1/2 cup Parmesan, 1 cup mozzarella, 1/2 tsp garlic powder and 1/2 tsp Italian seasoning.
steps: Heat oven to 375°F; lightly grease a 9×13-inch dish.
Cook beef and onion over medium-high 8–10 minutes; drain excess grease. Add garlic 30 seconds, then the meat-sauce seasonings 30 seconds.
Add both jars Ragu and simmer uncovered over medium-low 10–15 minutes. Add sugar only if the finished sauce tastes acidic.
Boil noodles al dente. Mix the cheese bowl.

Layer: thin sauce; 4 noodles; 1/3 sauce; half ricotta mixture; 1 cup mozzarella; 4 noodles; 1/3 sauce; remaining ricotta mixture; 1 cup mozzarella; 4 noodles; remaining sauce; final 1 cup mozzarella and 1/2 cup Parmesan.
Cover tightly with foil; bake 25 minutes. Uncover and bake 15–20 minutes more. Broil 1–2 minutes only if desired.
Rest 15–20 minutes before cutting.
note: Layers of seasoned beef sauce, mozzarella, Parmesan and a light ricotta filling baked until bubbling.
leftovers: Refrigerate promptly; reheat gently until hot.

name: Classic Beef Chili
ingredients: 2 cans (15 oz each) kidney beans, drained and rinsed
1 can (15 oz) pinto beans, drained and rinsed
prep: Pot — Beef: Dice onion; have beef and garlic ready.
Bowl — Seasoning: Combine all dry seasonings.
Open tomatoes and sauce; drain and rinse beans.
steps: Brown beef and onion over medium-high 8–10 minutes; drain excess grease.
Add garlic 30 seconds, then all dry seasonings for 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes, tomato sauce, broth and Worcestershire; stir in beans.
Bring to a gentle boil, reduce to low and simmer uncovered 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Taste after simmering before adding any extra salt.
note: Thick, meaty beef chili with beans, tomatoes and warm savory spices.
leftovers: Refrigerate promptly; reheat gently until hot.

name: Creamy White Chicken Chili
ingredients: 2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, bite-size pieces
2 cans (15 oz each) great northern beans, drained and rinsed
prep: Bowl 1 — Chicken: Toss chicken with oil and first four seasonings.
Pot additions: Dice onion; drain beans; measure chiles, broth, cumin, chili powder and corn.
Finish: Soften cream cheese; measure heavy cream.
steps: Brown seasoned chicken over medium-high 6–8 minutes to 165°F; remove.
Cook onion 4 minutes; add garlic 30 seconds.
Add broth, beans, chiles, cumin, chili powder and corn. Simmer 15 minutes.
Reduce heat to low; whisk in cream cheese, then heavy cream.
Return chicken and simmer gently 3–5 minutes. Do not hard-boil after adding dairy.
note: Creamy white chicken chili with tender chicken thighs, white beans, green chiles and corn.
leftovers: Refrigerate promptly; reheat gently until hot.

name: Beefy Chili Mac
prep: Skillet — Beef: Dice onion; measure beef, garlic and seasonings.
Sauce: Open tomato sauce and tomatoes; measure broth.
Finish: Measure macaroni and cheddar.
steps: Brown beef and onion over medium-high 7–9 minutes; drain excess grease.
Add garlic and seasonings; stir 30 seconds.
Add tomato sauce, tomatoes, broth and dry macaroni; bring to a simmer.
Cover, reduce to medium-low and cook 10–12 minutes, stirring once or twice, until pasta is tender.
Remove from heat; stir in 1 1/2 cups cheddar, top with remaining 1/2 cup and cover 2 minutes.
note: Ground beef, chili-seasoned tomato sauce, macaroni and melted cheddar in one pan.
leftovers: Refrigerate promptly; reheat gently until hot.

name: Hamburger Steaks & Onion Gravy
prep: Bowl 1 — Patties: Mix beef, egg, breadcrumbs, seasonings and 1 tsp Worcestershire; form 4 oval patties.
Onion: Slice onion.
Bowl 2 — Gravy: Measure butter, flour, broth and remaining Worcestershire.
steps: Cook patties over medium-high about 4–5 minutes per side; remove.
Reduce to medium; cook onion 6–8 minutes until browned.
Add butter, then flour; stir 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in broth and remaining Worcestershire. Simmer 3–5 minutes until thickened.
Return patties and simmer in gravy 2–3 minutes.
note: Seasoned hamburger steaks smothered in rich onion gravy.
leftovers: Refrigerate promptly; reheat gently until hot.

name: Saucy Sloppy Joes
prep: Skillet — Beef: Dice onion; measure beef, garlic and seasonings.
Bowl — Sauce: Mix ketchup, mustard, Worcestershire, brown sugar and broth.
Buns: Have 6 ready.
steps: Brown beef and onion over medium-high 7–9 minutes; drain excess grease.
Add garlic 30 seconds, then dry seasonings.
Pour in sauce mixture. Reduce to medium-low and simmer uncovered 8–10 minutes until thick enough to stay on a bun.
Taste after reducing, then spoon onto buns.
note: Saucy sweet-savory ground beef piled onto soft hamburger buns.
leftovers: Refrigerate promptly; reheat gently until hot.

name: Taco Beef & Rice Skillet
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
prep: Skillet — Beef: Dice onion; have beef and garlic ready.
Bowl — Seasoning: Combine chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, onion powder, seasoned salt and paprika.
Rice: Rinse rice; drain beans; measure broth, salsa and cheese.
steps: Brown beef and onion over medium-high 7–9 minutes; drain excess grease.
Add garlic 30 seconds; add seasoning mixture 30 seconds.
Stir in rice, broth, salsa and beans; bring to a simmer.
Cover, reduce to low and cook about 15 minutes until rice is tender.
Remove from heat, top with cheese and cover 2 minutes to melt.
note: Seasoned taco beef, rice, black beans, salsa and melted cheese cooked in one skillet.
leftovers: Refrigerate promptly; reheat gently until hot.

name: Classic Glazed Meatloaf
prep: Bowl 1 — Meatloaf: Combine beef, eggs, breadcrumbs, milk, onion, garlic, seasonings, Worcestershire and 1/2 cup ketchup.
Bowl 2 — Glaze: Mix remaining 1/2 cup ketchup, brown sugar and mustard.
Pan: Line a rimmed sheet pan or grease a loaf pan.
steps: Heat oven to 375°F.
Gently mix meatloaf ingredients only until combined. Shape into a loaf.
Spread half the glaze on top and bake 40 minutes.
Add remaining glaze and bake 15–20 minutes more, until center reaches 160°F.
Rest 10 minutes before slicing.
note: Classic tender meatloaf finished with a sweet-savory ketchup glaze.
leftovers: Refrigerate promptly; reheat gently until hot.

name: Cheesy Beef Enchiladas
prep: Skillet — Filling: Dice onion; measure beef, garlic and seasonings.
Assembly: Have sauce, tortillas and cheese ready.
Pan: Lightly grease a 9×13-inch dish.
steps: Heat oven to 375°F.
Brown beef and onion over medium-high 7–9 minutes; drain excess grease.
Add garlic 30 seconds, then seasonings 30 seconds. Remove from heat and stir in 1 cup cheese.
Spread a thin layer of enchilada sauce in pan. Divide beef among tortillas, roll and place seam-side down.
Pour remaining sauce over tortillas; top with remaining 1 1/2 cups cheese.
Cover with foil and bake 20 minutes. Uncover and bake 10 minutes more.
note: Seasoned beef and melted cheese rolled in tortillas and baked with red enchilada sauce.
leftovers: Refrigerate promptly; reheat gently until hot.
